title: Governor of Tennessee

context.text: Open seat: Republican Gov. Bill Lee is term-limited and cannot seek a third consecutive term.
Republican primary (Aug. 6): U.S. Sen. Marsha Blackburn won with about 44% of the vote, ahead of U.S. Rep. John Rose (about 33%) and state Rep. Monty Fritts (about 24%).
Democratic primary (Aug. 6): Memphis City Council member Jerri Green won with about 69% of the vote, ahead of Carnita Atwater (about 18%) and three other candidates.

Thirteen independents qualified for the November ballot by petition, making 15 governor candidates in total. They match the Tennessee Secretary of State's certified candidate list and the Davidson County sample ballot.

candidates.name: Marsha Blackburn
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Aug. 6 Republican primary with about 44% of the vote.

priorities.text: Keeping taxes low and growing the economy, building on her opposition to a state income tax.
Immigration enforcement: supporting mass deportations and keeping sanctuary cities out of Tennessee.
Parental rights and school choice, including fully implementing Tennessee's new school choice law.
Keeping men out of girls' and women's sports.

positions.summary: Her campaign says she is 100 percent pro-life and has supported legislation to help end federal funding of abortion.
Says she backs President Trump's immigration policy and mass deportations, and will ensure sanctuary cities never have a home in Tennessee.
positions.quote: Marsha backs President Trump's immigration policy 100 percent

positions.summary: Says she supports school choice and will fully implement Tennessee's new school choice law.
Says she introduced legislation to reverse federal rules that would let biological males compete in women's sports and will make sure girls' sports are protected.

record.text: Voted yes on the Laken Riley Act (S. 5), which passed the Senate 64–35.
Voted yes on H.R. 1 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act) in the Senate, which passed 50–50 with the Vice President breaking the tie.
Voted yes on the GENIUS Act (S. 1582), a stablecoin regulation bill that passed the Senate 68–30.

candidates.name: Jerri Green
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Aug. 6 Democratic primary with about 69% of the vote.

priorities.text: Day-one actions using federal TANF funds: waiving security deposits, clearing the child care waitlist and erasing medical debt.
Expanding Medicaid, protecting TennCare, and repealing Tennessee's near-total abortion ban.
Fully funding public schools rather than 'unaccountable voucher schemes', raising teacher pay and expanding universal pre-K.
Gun safety measures including universal background checks and red flag laws.

positions.summary: Platform says she would repeal Tennessee's near-total abortion ban and sign an executive order protecting doctors from prosecution.
Platform calls for universal background checks on all gun sales, red flag laws, closing domestic violence loopholes and free gun locks.
Would sign an executive order on day one to end Tennessee Highway Patrol and law enforcement cooperation with ICE and ban ICE from state buildings.
Would expand Medicaid to cover more working families, keep rural hospitals open and protect TennCare.
Platform says she would fully fund K-12 public education 'not siphon dollars into unaccountable voucher schemes'.
Day-one plan uses $50 million of TANF funds to clear the child care waitlist; platform also proposes universal pre-K and more affordable child care.
Platform calls for investing in renewable energy and green jobs and enforcing clean air and water standards.

record.text: Sponsored Memphis Ordinance No. 5906 to let the City Court Clerk's office accept partial payments for traffic citations; it was approved on second reading.

Her campaign site says she launched Tennessee's first free gun lock-by-mail program in Memphis and led an effort to clear $17 million in medical debt for 12,000 Memphians (campaign claims, not independently verified).

candidates.name: David Hatley

priorities.text: Reading and workforce training: a goal of reaching the top ten nationally in reading within four years, with full-time reading coaches in the state's 100 lowest-performing elementary schools, and doubling registered apprenticeships in four years.
Eliminating the state sales tax on groceries, paid for by cutting waste in the state budget.
Creating a state-regulated medical cannabis program.

positions.summary: His campaign site says letting male-bodied athletes compete in women's categories takes opportunities from girls, and that Tennessee law should reflect that.
positions.quote: Women’s spaces should be for women — and that includes locker rooms and teams.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he would support rewriting Tennessee's handgun-carry law so that lawful carry by law-abiding adults is the default, with narrow restrictions.
positions.quote: As governor I’d support rewriting that law so lawful handgun carry by law-abiding adults is the default, with restrictions that are specific, narrow, and consistent with Bruen

positions.summary: His campaign site says he would keep current voucher recipients enrolled but hold the program at its current size and publish data, rather than expand it.
positions.quote: I will hold the program at its current size and publish the data: who is receiving the money, where it is going, and how those students are performing.

statements.quote: If someone is here illegally and commits violent crimes, they shouldn’t be in our communities, and the state should be working to see they aren’t.
The price is high because there are not enough seats. So the fix is to build more of them.
statements.context: Under 'Child Care' on his campaign website

statements.quote: Housing: Make It Cheaper to Build the Smaller House.
statements.context: Heading of his housing plan on his campaign website

statements.quote: Healthcare should be about keeping people healthy, not profiting off them getting sick.
statements.context: Under 'Rural Healthcare' on his campaign website

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements are from the policy sections of his campaign website (hatleyforgovernor.com). Nothing found on rent regulation, climate, minimum wage, tariffs or taxes on high earners.

candidates.name: Lauren Pinkston

priorities.text: Agriculture and education, including support for Tennessee farmers, limiting data and benchmark tests in teaching, and workforce development.
Repealing Tennessee's 4% state grocery tax, which she says the state is 'perfectly capable' of doing.

statements.quote: We live in a modern society, and so while we can have Tennessee first and America first policies, we don’t make those policies in a vacuum
statements.context: Speaking about farmers affected by federal tariffs, per the Tennessee Lookout, Nov. 2025

statements.quote: Ultimately, health care decisions should lie with the patient and the doctor, and the issues of morality need to have social supports around them so we can save as many lives as possible in this state
statements.context: Speaking to the Tennessee Lookout, Sept. 2026; the article also reports she 'believes all life is sacred' and has criticized the state's abortion ban

candidates.researchNotes: Her campaign site (pinkstonfortn.com) returned a bot-verification page and could not be read. Statements come from three news interviews (Tennessee Lookout twice, Lebanon Democrat). The Lookout reports she supports repealing the voucher program, but gives no quote from her, so it is not recorded as a position.

candidates.name: Misam Abidi

priorities.text: A seven-point plan: blockchain and technology economy, a Tennessee Dividend Fund, healthcare affordability, a skills guarantee for students, due process, recovery reform and human-centered governance.

statements.context: Listed as a key goal under 'Healthcare Affordability Reform' on his campaign website

candidates.researchNotes: Positions are from the seven pillars on his campaign website; none takes a side on the guide's issue statements, so only statements are shown. His rental-housing line is about homeownership, not rent regulation, so it is not shown.

candidates.name: Dean Brewer
candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, questionnaire or news interview found. A Facebook post is quoted in an independent voter-guide blog, which is not used as a source here.

candidates.name: Ray Brown
candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, questionnaire or news interview found. A statement attributed to him appears only in an independent voter-guide blog, which is not used as a source here.

candidates.name: Wendell Jackson

priorities.text: Employment services, housing stability and healthcare for all, plus support for local businesses.

statements.quote: ensure healthcare and housing for all
statements.context: From the home page of his campaign website

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign website gives broad goals and links to unreadable video interviews; one statement on an ISSUES topic was found, so research depth stays minimal.

candidates.name: Charles Van Morgan
candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, questionnaire or quoted statements found; the WJHL candidate profile returned an access-denied page.

candidates.name: Eddie Lee Murphy
candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, questionnaire or news coverage of his governor campaign found; Ballotpedia shows no Candidate Connection survey for him.

candidates.name: Victor L. Scoggin

priorities.text: Funding law enforcement, restoring Second Amendment and voting rights to non-violent felons, justice system reform, homelessness and mental illness, property tax reform, and healthcare.

positions.summary: His campaign site lists funding law enforcement among the major issues in Tennessee.

statements.context: Item 6 on his campaign website's list of major issues in Tennessee

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign site lists seven issues in a few words each, without describing specific proposals; only items that map to the guide's issues are shown.

candidates.name: Dave Seeman

priorities.text: Climate action, including state-owned renewable power, public transportation and support for farmers.
Economic stability: ending the state grocery tax, a higher minimum wage and permanently affordable housing.
Funding for children and families, including ending school vouchers and covering childcare for incomes under $99,000.
Government accountability: audits of state programs over $25 million, open data and independent redistricting.

positions.summary: His platform proposes universal background checks, safe-storage requirements and a court process to temporarily remove firearms from someone in crisis.
positions.quote: Require background checks on every firearm sale, require safe storage when kids are in the home, and create a court-ordered process for temporarily removing firearms from someone in crisis.

positions.summary: His platform proposes repealing Tennessee laws that require sheriffs to act on federal immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: Repeal the laws that force every Tennessee sheriff to act as a federal immigration agent, so officers can focus on the cases their communities actually need them on.

positions.summary: His platform proposes allowing duplexes by right.
positions.quote: We'll also make it legal to build a duplex.

positions.summary: His platform proposes worldwide combined reporting for multistate corporations and restoring the franchise tax base, to pay for ending the grocery tax.
positions.quote: We'll require worldwide combined reporting and restore the franchise tax base the legislature gave away in 2024, redesigned to hold up in court, so every corporation profiting in Tennessee pays its share.

positions.summary: His platform proposes covering poor adults through a federal waiver and fully expanding TennCare once federal funding is confirmed.
positions.quote: Cover Tennessee's poorest adults now through a federal waiver, and expand TennCare fully the day Washington confirms that expanding won't cut the hospital fund.

positions.summary: His platform proposes repealing Tennessee's private school voucher program.
positions.quote: Repeal Tennessee's private school voucher and spend every dollar of it on the working conditions that decide whether good teachers stay in the schools that lose them fastest.

positions.summary: His platform proposes raising Tennessee's minimum wage from $12 to $21 an hour over four years.
positions.quote: Raise Tennessee's minimum wage to $21 an hour over four years, starting at $12 the first year, and let cities set their own wage floors above the state level.

statements.quote: Making abortions illegal doesn't stop them. It makes them costlier, riskier, and later, the opposite of what the law claimed to protect.
statements.context: On his campaign platform page, under 'Restore Medical Privacy'

statements.quote: We'll also take gas fueling stations and gas-fired heat and power plants off the state's certified green energy list, including existing certifications, so that neither gets tax breaks reserved for clean energy.
Cover childcare costs for every working Tennessee family earning up to $99,000, with parents free to choose center-based, home-based, or faith-based providers.
provide tariff buffer grants so trade disruptions don't wipe out Tennessee farmers.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements are from his campaign platform (davefortn.com), which describes him as the Green Party candidate; the state ballot lists him as Independent. Nothing found on rent regulation, proof of citizenship for voting, transgender athletes or war powers.

candidates.name: Karl Knox Smithson
candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, questionnaire or news coverage found; Ballotpedia shows no Candidate Connection survey for him.

candidates.name: L. Webb Taylor
candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, questionnaire or news coverage found; Ballotpedia shows no Candidate Connection survey for him.

candidates.name: Robert C. Vick

priorities.text: 'Rural Readiness': aligning high school curricula with local industry needs, expanding rural healthcare access and addressing the root causes of the opioid crisis.
Applying debt-free budgeting principles to state government and prioritizing core functions such as education, infrastructure and safety.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he is concerned about universal school vouchers and would take a 'public first' approach, while respecting parents' right to choose private or home schooling.
positions.quote: Vouchers drain money from the local schools that serve as the heartbeat of these communities.

statements.quote: I support those that wish to start a new life in America, but like my mom, everyone needs to come and document it as our legal system requires.
statements.context: On his campaign website's issues page

statements.quote: Protecting At-Risk Facilities: Moving beyond temporary grants to create sustainable, long-term funding models that keep rural ERs and maternity wards open.
statements.context: On his campaign website's issues page

statements.quote: Support Law Enforcement: Providing our officers with the training and resources they need
statements.context: On his campaign website's issues page

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements are from his campaign issues page and a Greeneville Sun article on his announcement. Nothing found on abortion, guns, rent, minimum wage or taxes on high earners.

researchNotes: The 15-candidate slate matches the Tennessee Secretary of State's certified Governor candidate list (Nov. 3, 2026 general election) and the Davidson County Election Commission sample ballot exactly, including party lines and home cities. Blackburn's positions are from her campaign issue pages and Green's and Hatley's from their campaign sites; only positions stated directly there are listed. Minimal-tier summaries for independents rely on The Tennessee Firefly (which draws on Politics1, campaign sites and Ballotpedia) because Ballotpedia could not be read; occupation descriptions that the Firefly could not corroborate are stated as 'listed as'. Primary-result percentages come from Wikipedia's results tables. Misam Abidi's federal indictment is reported as a charge only: the IRS Criminal Investigation release, WREG and WSMV were read directly, and neither news report was found to state a plea or verdict.
